module_title: Gandhian Era and Mass Movements (1919-1939) - Basic Understanding
introduction: Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in 1915. His arrival marked the beginning of a new phase in the Indian National Movement, known as the 'Gandhian Era'. He introduced the concept of 'Satyagraha' (based on truth and non-violence) and transformed the national movement from an elite struggle into a mass movement.

core_concepts.title: Gandhi's Early Satyagrahas
core_concepts.description: Before launching national movements, Gandhi successfully led three local struggles: Champaran (1917, for indigo farmers), Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918, for mill workers), and Kheda (1918, for peasants).

core_concepts.title: Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh (1919)
core_concepts.description: The British passed the 'Rowlatt Act' allowing arrest without trial. In protest, a peaceful gathering was held at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar on April 13, 1919, where General Dyer ordered troops to open fire on the unarmed crowd.

core_concepts.title: Khilafat Movement (1919-1920)
core_concepts.description: Started by the Ali Brothers (Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali) to protest against the injustice done to the Caliph of Turkey after WWI. Gandhi saw this as a golden opportunity to unite Hindus and Muslims.

core_concepts.title: Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-1922)
core_concepts.description: This was Gandhi's first all-India mass movement. It involved the surrender of British titles, and the boycott of government schools, law courts, and foreign cloth.

core_concepts.title: Chauri Chaura Incident (1922)
core_concepts.description: On February 5, 1922, an angry mob set fire to a police station in Chauri Chaura (UP), killing 22 policemen. Deeply hurt by this violence, Gandhi abruptly called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.

important_entities.name: Mahatma Gandhi
important_entities.significance: United the Indian masses using the tools of Satyagraha and Ahimsa (non-violence).

important_entities.name: General Dyer
important_entities.significance: The officer responsible for the brutal Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

important_entities.name: Rabindranath Tagore
important_entities.significance: Renounced his 'Knighthood' in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often confuse the order of Kheda and Ahmedabad. Remember that the Ahmedabad Mill Strike (Feb-March 1918) happened just before the Kheda Satyagraha (March 1918).
Champaran was Gandhi's first 'Civil Disobedience' in India, but his first 'Hunger Strike' was during the Ahmedabad Mill Strike.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: C - Champaran, A - Ahmedabad, K - Kheda, E - Early movements.

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize the exact date of the Chauri Chaura incident (Feb 5, 1922) and the movement it halted (Non-Cooperation).
The Rowlatt Act was famously called the 'Black Act' (No Dalil, No Vakil, No Appeal). Focus on its draconian provisions.
